items.stem: Define the term “an ecosystem”.
items.answer: A functional unit of nature where living organisms interact among themselves and with their surrounding physical environment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a functional unit of nature where living organisms interact among themselves and with their surrounding physical environment.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about ecosystem structure, function and productivity is correct?
items.answer: The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter.
items.markingKey: (b) The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. The other statements are false. NPP = GPP − R. Oceans cover about 70% of the surface but produce only 55 of the 170 billion tons. Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.
options: Secondary productivity is the rate of photosynthesis.
The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter.
Oceans have the highest productivity of the biosphere because they are the largest.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Secondary productivity is the rate of photosynthesis.
Reason (R): Trees occupy the top vertical strata of a forest, shrubs the second and herbs and grasses the bottom layers.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “NPP = GPP + R.”
items.answer: NPP = GPP − R.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: NPP = GPP − R.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): NPP is less than GPP.
Reason (R): Plants use part of the GPP in respiration.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) NPP = GPP − R.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
A school group in Bhopal compares a grassland plot with a deep lake of the same area.
(i) What is primary productivity? (1 mark)
(ii) Give two factors on which it depends. (1 mark)
(iii) Oceans cover 70% of the earth, yet their productivity is about 55 of 170 billion tons. Explain. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The rate of biomass production per unit area over a time period by plants. (ii) Plant species, environmental factors, availability of nutrients, photosynthetic capacity (any two). (iii) In the open ocean, nutrients (especially nitrogen) are scarce and light penetrates only the upper layers, so productivity per unit area is low.

items.stem: Which of the following is a consumer in a pond ecosystem?
items.answer: bottom-dwelling fishes
items.markingKey: (b) Bottom-dwelling fishes is a consumer in a pond ecosystem; the others are not.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Oceans have the highest productivity of the biosphere because they are the largest.”
items.answer: Oceans cover about 70% of the surface but produce only 55 of the 170 billion tons.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Oceans cover about 70% of the surface but produce only 55 of the 170 billion tons.

items.stem: Which term describes the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis?
items.answer: primary production
items.markingKey: (b) Primary production: the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis.

Which of the following is NOT a consumer in a pond ecosystem?
items.answer: fungi
items.markingKey: (d) Fungi is a decomposer in a pond ecosystem, not a consumer in a pond ecosystem.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a decomposer in a pond ecosystem?
items.answer: phytoplankton
items.markingKey: (d) Phytoplankton is a producer in a pond ecosystem, not a decomposer in a pond ecosystem.

items.stem: Distinguish between gross and net primary productivity. Why is NPP important?
items.answer: GPP is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis; a considerable part of it is used by plants in respiration. NPP = GPP − R. NPP is the biomass available for consumption by heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers), so it determines how much energy flows to higher trophic levels.
items.markingKey: 1 mark difference; 1 mark importance.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Secondary productivity is the rate of photosynthesis.”
items.answer: Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.

items.stem: Define the term “net primary productivity (NPP)”.
items.answer: GPP minus respiration losses; the biomass available for consumption by heterotrophs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: GPP minus respiration losses; the biomass available for consumption by heterotrophs.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as consumer in a pond ecosystem or producer in a pond ecosystem: floating and submerged plants, free-swimming fishes, some algae, phytoplankton.
items.answer: floating and submerged plants – producer in a pond ecosystem; free-swimming fishes – consumer in a pond ecosystem; some algae – producer in a pond ecosystem; phytoplankton – producer in a pond ecosystem.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: floating and submerged plants – producer in a pond ecosystem; free-swimming fishes – consumer in a pond ecosystem; some algae – producer in a pond ecosystem; phytoplankton – producer in a pond ecosystem.

items.stem: What is meant by “detritus”?
items.answer: Dead plant remains such as leaves, bark and flowers, and dead remains of animals including faecal matter.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: dead plant remains such as leaves, bark and flowers, and dead remains of animals including faecal matter.

items.stem:
Aditi keeps two compost pits on her farm near Nashik: one of kitchen peels kept moist and warm, the other of dry sawdust.
(i) Which pit decomposes faster? (1 mark)
(ii) Name the step in which earthworms act. (1 mark)
(iii) Give two reasons for the difference in rates. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The moist pit with kitchen peels. (ii) Fragmentation. (iii) Kitchen peels are rich in nitrogen and water-soluble sugars while sawdust is rich in lignin; warm, moist and aerated conditions favour decomposer activity.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct steps of decomposition: leaching, humification, mineralisation, catabolism. Give a reason.
items.answer: leaching → catabolism → humification → mineralisation

items.stem: Why does organic matter accumulate in the soil of cold, waterlogged regions?
items.answer: Low temperature reduces the activity of decomposers and waterlogging creates anaerobic conditions; since decomposition is largely an oxygen-requiring process, it is inhibited and organic material builds up.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each factor.

items.stem:
In a grassland near Jaipur, grass fixes 20,000 J, which passes to grasshoppers, then frogs, then snakes.
(i) State the 10 per cent law. (1 mark)
(ii) How much energy reaches the snakes? (1 mark)
(iii) Why are food chains rarely longer than four or five links? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Only about 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next. (ii) 20,000 → 2000 → 200 → 20 J. (iii) Energy available decreases by about 90% at each level, being lost as heat in respiration, so after four or five levels too little energy is left to support another level.

items.stem: Distinguish between the grazing food chain and the detritus food chain.
items.answer: GFC starts from producers (grass → goat → man) and is the main conduit of energy in aquatic ecosystems. DFC begins with dead organic matter, made of decomposers (fungi, bacteria) that get energy from detritus; in terrestrial ecosystems a larger fraction of energy flows through the DFC.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: What are ecological pyramids? Describe the pyramids of number, biomass and energy with one example each where it is inverted or always upright. Give two limitations of pyramids.
items.answer: Graphic representations of the relationship between organisms at different trophic levels, with producers at the base. Number: upright in a grassland, inverted in a tree ecosystem. Biomass: upright in most terrestrial ecosystems, inverted in the sea (fish biomass > phytoplankton). Energy: always upright, as energy decreases at each level. Limitations: they do not consider the same species at two or more trophic levels; they assume a simple food chain and do not accommodate food webs; saprophytes are not given a place.
items.markingKey: 1 mark definition; 3 marks pyramids; 1 mark limitations.

items.stem: Name the step of decomposition in which a dark amorphous substance called humus, highly resistant to microbial action, accumulates.
items.answer: humification
items.markingKey: (c) Humification: a dark amorphous substance called humus, highly resistant to microbial action, accumulates.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The number of trophic levels in a food chain is limited.
Reason (R): Only about 10% of energy is transferred to the next level.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Too little energy remains after 4–5 levels.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about ecosystem structure, function and productivity is correct?
items.answer: Trees occupy the top vertical strata of a forest, shrubs the second and herbs and grasses the bottom layers.
items.markingKey: (a) Trees occupy the top vertical strata of a forest, shrubs the second and herbs and grasses the bottom layers. The other statements are false. NPP = GPP − R. Oceans cover about 70% of the surface but produce only 55 of the 170 billion tons. Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.
options: Trees occupy the top vertical strata of a forest, shrubs the second and herbs and grasses the bottom layers.
Oceans have the highest productivity of the biosphere because they are the largest.
Secondary productivity is the rate of photosynthesis.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct steps of decomposition: mineralisation, catabolism, leaching, fragmentation. Give a reason.
items.answer: fragmentation → leaching → catabolism → mineralisation
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order fragmentation → leaching → catabolism → mineralisation; 1 mark for the reason: Fragmentation, leaching and catabolism operate simultaneously; humification and mineralisation occur in the soil.

items.stem: Which term describes a sequence of organisms through which energy flows by one eating another?
items.answer: a food chain
items.markingKey: (d) A food chain: a sequence of organisms through which energy flows by one eating another.

items.stem: Name the step of decomposition in which a dark amorphous substance called humus, highly resistant to microbial action, accumulates.
items.answer: humification
items.markingKey: (d) Humification: a dark amorphous substance called humus, highly resistant to microbial action, accumulates.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as consumer in a pond ecosystem or decomposer in a pond ecosystem: free-swimming fishes, zooplankton, flagellates, bottom-dwelling fishes.
items.answer: free-swimming fishes – consumer in a pond ecosystem; zooplankton – consumer in a pond ecosystem; flagellates – decomposer in a pond ecosystem; bottom-dwelling fishes – consumer in a pond ecosystem.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: free-swimming fishes – consumer in a pond ecosystem; zooplankton – consumer in a pond ecosystem; flagellates – decomposer in a pond ecosystem; bottom-dwelling fishes – consumer in a pond ecosystem.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about energy flow and ecological pyramids is incorrect?
items.answer: The pyramid of biomass in the sea is upright.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “The pyramid of biomass in the sea is upright.” Correct form: It is generally inverted because the biomass of fishes exceeds that of phytoplankton.
options: The pyramid of biomass in the sea is upright.
Ecological pyramids do not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels.
In an aquatic ecosystem the GFC is the major conduit for energy flow.
The pyramid of energy is always upright.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about decomposition is correct?
items.answer: Low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit decomposition, leading to build-up of organic material.
items.markingKey: (a) Low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit decomposition, leading to build-up of organic material. The other statements are false. Lignin and chitin slow decomposition. Warm and moist conditions favour it. Leaching carries soluble nutrients down where they precipitate as unavailable salts.
options: Low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit decomposition, leading to build-up of organic material.
Decomposition is faster in cold, dry conditions.
Decomposition is faster when detritus is rich in lignin and chitin.
Leaching makes nutrients available near the soil surface.

items.stem: A field receives 10 × 10⁶ J of incident solar radiation. If photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) is 50% of this and plants capture 5% of PAR, how much energy is captured by the plants?
A tertiary consumer receives 10 kJ of energy. Applying the 10 per cent law, how much energy must have been fixed by the producers?
items.markingKey: (a) The tertiary consumer is trophic level 4; energy at producers = 10 × 10^3 = 10000 kJ.

items.stem: Explain the term “the grazing food chain (GFC)”.
items.answer: A food chain that starts with producers, such as grass → goat → man.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a food chain that starts with producers, such as grass → goat → man.
